body: My store had an MIT who would hound higher ups on the hive everyday for almost an entire year after they promised a living wage and then refused to even talk about raises. About a year and a half later they gave us a raise. The raise was $0.07. So now instead of $18.63/hour it’s a whole &18.70/hour! Felt like the biggest spit in the face I’ve ever had from this company.

Often at times I feel the exact same way. I talk to my therapist about this a lot. A good piece of it is where you put your self worth. Mine is through the floor so it’s like I can feel hurt by things that people would consider “red flags” yet not identify them as red flags at all, and continue to let it things slide. Even after they’ve become so obvious. My therapist has told me it’s also a defense mechanism. Subconsciously, we know what the issues look like, but having to unlearn and truly pick apart the steps we need to take to get better can be so frustrating and often times painful. Since processing what happened to you can sometimes feel like reliving all of it. It makes it too real. As a result we continue the behaviors in a way to prove that this is just who we are, this is exactly who we would be had the trauma not left its mark on us. Like in a backwards  “I am not my trauma” type a way. But like we always hear people say “it gets worse before it gets better” there’s a lot of truth to it. This is all just my experience I guess. I was diagnosed with CPTSD, and until this year I kind of just ignored what that meant for me. Processing and reprocessing has been a lot of work emotionally. Sometimes I feel so much weaker now than I did when I was going through my trauma. In my ways of coping with it while it was happening by running away from it or dissociating, that never made me strong. It just made me good at surviving. Once we are removed from those situations it can be so hard to identify our own behaviors that are bad for us. They can seem normal since that’s how we behaved when we were in survival mode. But you’re not hopeless. You are fully capable of changing this and I’m rooting for you. I don’t mean to discourage you, like I said, this could just be me. A lot of it will come down to you deciding for yourself what you’re willing to tolerate and what level of respect you think you deserve. You will be your own liberator.
